learningObjectives: Understand how this course is organized: 5 sections (Introduction & Theory, REST, SOAP, Self-Created SOAP, XML) covering 12 lessons.
Confirm the prerequisites: a basic understanding of APIs, completion of Tricentis Tosca Fundamentals (AS1), and access to a valid Tosca license.
Know that the API Scan is a standalone program that needs no Tosca license or installation to operate on its own.
Understand what you earn at the end of the course and how the Final Exam is structured.

elements.text: "Tricentis Tosca Deep Dive - Automating API test cases" covers Tricentis Tosca's standalone solution, the API Scan, which enables automated testing of application programming interfaces. The course covers how to use the API Scan to gather the technical information of your API and how to add the relevant business information to run your tests. It also explores automation techniques for REST APIs, SOAP APIs, and XML files.

elements.title: By the end of this course, you will be able to:
items: Create Modules and Test Cases using the API Scan for API testing in Tricentis Tosca.
Create Modules and Test Cases using the API Scan for XML and JSON file testing in Tricentis Tosca.
Describe the difference between SOAP and REST APIs.
Scan XML files in the API Scan.

bulletPoints: This content was developed using Tosca 12.x — minor UI differences are possible in other versions.
The course is delivered across 16 syllabus sections and 51 lessons totaling about 4 hours.

rows: Tour the Swagger UI, learn the general process of automating Webservices, and learn the technical terminology behind API and XML test automation.
Tour the default view of the API Scan and automate a REST Scan imported into Tosca Commander.
Automate a complete SOAP Scan and a self-created SOAP Message exported from the API Scan.
Learn additional functionalities of the API Scan, including automating XML files using the Tricentis Tosca Standard Modules.
Prove your knowledge of all topics covered in the course.

elements.text: In total, the course material is covered through lesson videos and exercise solution videos, and requires completing 12 hands-on practical exercises within Tricentis Tosca (numbered Exercise 01 through Exercise 12b).

elements.description: The API Scan is also a standalone program (ApiScanStandalone.exe). No Tosca license is needed and no Tosca installation or testing knowledge is required to operate the API Scan by itself. This makes it easy to involve developers in the testing process: send them the .exe file, they scan the API, save the resulting messages, and send them back as a subset that can be manipulated and tested — without installing or activating the full Tosca package.

elements.text: Throughout this course, the API Scan is always opened from inside Tricentis Tosca itself (Home ribbon > API Testing tab), rather than the standalone .exe, since every exercise exports results into Tosca Commander.

bulletPoints: No license or Tosca install is required to run the API Scan standalone — only to export results into Tosca Commander.
This is a shift-left tool: developers can scan and share API messages before a UI even exists.

elements.term: Tosca keeps showing a license pop-up on launch?
elements.description: This usually means Tosca Commander isn't connected to a valid license source. Since every exercise in this course exports API Scan results into Tosca Commander, a working license connection is required even though the API Scan itself needs none. If your organization uses a Cloud License Server, connect Tosca directly to it.

elements.title: Connect to your Cloud License Server
items: Double-check with your administrator that you've been added to the Cloud License Server — you can only connect to servers you have a user account on.
In Tosca Commander, access the license configuration, go to the Setup tab, and select Change connection.
On the next screen, select Connect to Cloud hosted License Server, then click OK.
On the next screen, sign in with your Tricentis Support Hub credentials. If your organization uses a proxy server, activate the Use default proxy checkbox on the sign-in screen.
A successful connection takes you directly to the Tosca start screen — the license pop-up should not reappear.

items.label: Connect to your cloud license server

bulletPoints: Still stuck? Check with your Tosca administrator whether your account has been granted access to the specific Cloud License Server your organization uses.

elements.description: Application Programming Interface — an interface created with the application in mind rather than the user. Where a UI is designed to be human-readable, an API is machine-readable: it speaks the language of the software directly.

elements.title: Why test through the API instead of only the UI:
items: API TestCases execute faster than the equivalent manual or UI-automated test — no UI loading times to wait through.
Testing can start earlier in the development lifecycle: APIs are often defined and built before a UI exists, which fits Agile/shift-left practices.
Many UI-automation challenges (control identification, screen resolution, load timing) simply don't apply to API testing.
Maintenance is lighter: instead of rescripting tests by hand, you re-scan the changed parts of the API and reuse or adapt existing artifacts.

elements.text: Historically, API testing meant developers hand-coding and hand-maintaining scripts. The API Scan removes most of that manual scripting and maintenance burden, bringing developers and QAs closer together in the same testing process.

bulletPoints: API testing bypasses UI load times, so far more tests can run in the same timeframe.
Because APIs can be tested before a UI exists, defects are found earlier and more cheaply.

elements.text: This course ends with a Final Exam covering all topics from the course. As with the AS1/AS2 tracks, Tricentis Academy course completions typically earn a Badge with points rather than a standalone Certificate — Certificates are reserved for Tricentis's multi-course "Product Consultant" learning paths.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming the API Scan needs a Tosca license
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume every part of this course requires an activated Tosca license, since the exercises run inside Tosca Commander.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The API Scan itself is a standalone program — no license, no Tosca installation, and no testing knowledge are required to operate it alone. A license is only needed to export the scan results into Tosca Commander for automation.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing this course with AS1/AS2
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume this course re-teaches general Tosca UI automation basics.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: This course assumes AS1 (Tricentis Tosca Fundamentals) is already completed and builds specifically on API Scan functionality — REST, SOAP, self-created SOAP, and XML — not general UI TestCase construction.

examPitfalls.title: Thinking API testing replaces UI testing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates think the course argues API testing should replace UI testing entirely.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: API testing complements UI testing — it's faster and can start earlier in development, especially for functionality with no UI (or before a UI exists), not a wholesale replacement for UI automation.
